alerts.title: EFV CNS toxicity: insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines list dizziness, insomnia, abnormal dreams, and mental symptoms including suicidality as persistent CNS toxicity of EFV, recommending dose reduction to EFV 400mg. Patient on EFV since Feb 2024 reports poor sleep and vivid dreams for weeks. EFV is the likely cause given the classic symptom profile and temporal relationship. No suicidal ideation is present, but symptoms warrant action. Non-drug causes are less likely given the absence of other exam findings.

evidence.recommended_action: Lower EFV dose to 400mg. If symptoms persist after dose reduction, substitute EFV with DTG or another appropriate agent per guidelines.

alerts.title: Clinician plan lacks intervention for EFV toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend lowering EFV to 400mg for persistent CNS toxicity. The clinician's plan documents insomnia and vivid dreams but includes no medicine changes, orders, or any intervention. This is a plan gap — the assessment correctly identifies EFV-related symptoms but the plan does not act on them.

evidence.recommended_action: Add EFV dose reduction to 400mg to the plan, or substitute EFV with DTG if symptoms are severe or persistent despite prior dose adjustment.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring may be overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines require adults to have VL at 6 and 12 months after ART initiation, then every 12 months if suppressed. Patient started ART in Feb 2024; last VL was 2025-08-10 (60 copies/mL). The next annual VL would be due around Aug 2026, so monitoring appears on schedule. However, no baseline renal or hepatic labs are recorded for a TDF-containing regimen.

evidence.recommended_action: Confirm next VL is scheduled around Aug 2026. Ensure baseline and periodic renal and hepatic monitoring for TDF and EFV are performed.

Compared to clinical or immunological monitoring, 244

Consolidated Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of HIV and Aids in Uganda - 2022 virological monitoring provides an early and more accurate indication of treatment failure and indicates the need to switch from first line to second-line drugs, and from second- line to third-line drugs, toward reducing accumulation of drug-resistance mutations and improved clinical outcomes. Dolutegravir (DTG)-based regimens (e.g., tenofovir/lamivudine/dolutegravir [TLD]) have increased viral load suppression (VLS) rates to unprecedented levels, hence a need to actively monitor patients for low-level viremia to keep DTG a durable treatment option for as long as possible. Furthermore, low-level viraemia monitoring can enhances monitoring of achieving and sustaining HIV epidemic control, as viral load of >200 copies/mL is associated with potential risk of sexual transmission as well as subsequent virologic non-suppression and treatment failure.
